cohort: The participants were 15 surgical and non-surgical Caesarean section providers who worked at public hospitals in Sierra Leone during the 2014-2016 Ebola outbreak.
finding: Individual Caesarean section providers in Sierra Leone continued to perform surgeries during the Ebola epidemic due to their clinical adaptability to material limitations and their ability to overcome moral dilemmas despite the risk of infection.
mod_finding: Staff at public hospitals tended to prioritise performing Caesarean section surgery for women with acute obstetric complications during the Ebola outbreak.
